name: tokens
description: Color palette (Radix step roles), theme mapping, spacing, base styles, component classes and utilities. Import styles/index.css after tailwindcss

files.content:
/* better giving design-token palette. single source for color across the
   monorepo: the platform stylesheet `@import`s this verbatim for `:root`,
   and `colors.ts` mirrors it as hex for the email templates
   (mail clients strip stylesheets and don't support oklch()).

   the palette is light-only: the product ships no theme toggle, never applies
   `.dark` to any element, and has no prefers-color-scheme query — a dark half
   would double the cost of every palette change for no user-visible benefit.
   this is a decision, not an oversight: don't derive one without a product
   decision to ship dark mode first. see design-system.md. */

/* semantic design tokens — shadcn convention */

:root {
  /* the generated ramp — radix colors' custom-palette tool, driven from the
     brand blue with #e2e8f0 as the gray input and white as the background:
     https://www.radix-ui.com/colors/custom?accent-light=1E6DAB&gray-light=E2E8F0&background-light=FFFFFF
     step 9 of each accent scale is its input hex unmodified, which is what keeps
     the brand color where it is. the tool renames a scale after the nearest
     stock radix hue and emitted amber as orange; amber is the name here.

     each step is authored as the oklch() its source hex converts to, and the
     trailing comment is that source hex — colors.test.ts converts one back into
     the other, so a hand-tuned step fails the suite. a step is generated output:
     nothing here is nudged, and a value the ramp doesn't have is a gap to take
     back to the palette, not one to author.

     no alpha (-a1 … -a12) steps: the email mirror has no alpha channel. */

  --blue-1: oklch(0.992 0.004 236.5); /* #fafdff */
  --blue-2: oklch(0.979 0.01 247.9); /* #f3f9ff */
  --blue-3: oklch(0.959 0.023 237.6); /* #e4f4ff */
  --blue-4: oklch(0.934 0.035 240.3); /* #d5edff */
  --blue-5: oklch(0.902 0.051 245.7); /* #c4e3ff */
  --blue-6: oklch(0.861 0.066 247.9); /* #b0d6fb */
  --blue-7: oklch(0.806 0.082 247.2); /* #95c5f2 */
  --blue-8: oklch(0.731 0.109 247.3); /* #6daee9 */
  --blue-9: oklch(0.52 0.1225 247.31); /* #1e6dab */
  --blue-10: oklch(0.473 0.123 247.25); /* #055f9c */
  --blue-11: oklch(0.526 0.122 247.1); /* #206fad */
  --blue-12: oklch(0.35 0.065 248.2); /* #1c3d5b */

  --red-1: oklch(0.993 0.003 17.2); /* #fffcfc */
  --red-2: oklch(0.982 0.009 26); /* #fff7f6 */
  --red-3: oklch(0.955 0.022 24.4); /* #ffebe9 */
  --red-4: oklch(0.92 0.041 27.2); /* #ffdbd6 */
  --red-5: oklch(0.89 0.058 26.2); /* #ffcdc7 */
  --red-6: oklch(0.857 0.077 25.7); /* #ffbdb6 */
  --red-7: oklch(0.808 0.093 25.8); /* #f7a9a1 */
  --red-8: oklch(0.744 0.119 25.4); /* #ee8d85 */
  --red-9: oklch(0.541 0.208 25.4); /* #cc1926 */
  --red-10: oklch(0.498 0.203 26.4); /* #bb0016 */
  --red-11: oklch(0.557 0.208 25.4); /* #d2222b */
  --red-12: oklch(0.338 0.114 25.2); /* #661516 */

  --green-1: oklch(0.994 0.004 157.2); /* #fbfefc */
  --green-2: oklch(0.982 0.009 161.4); /* #f4fbf7 */
  --green-3: oklch(0.959 0.02 164.6); /* #e6f6ee */
  --green-4: oklch(0.933 0.032 163.2); /* #d7f0e3 */
  --green-5: oklch(0.901 0.044 163.1); /* #c5e8d6 */
  --green-6: oklch(0.859 0.057 162.7); /* #b0ddc6 */
  --green-7: oklch(0.8 0.074 162.8); /* #92cdb0 */
  --green-8: oklch(0.72 0.098 163.1); /* #66b893 */
  --green-9: oklch(0.568 0.1195 163.02); /* #0e8c62 */
  --green-10: oklch(0.524 0.115 161.9); /* #007e55 */
  --green-11: oklch(0.53 0.116 162.2); /* #008057 */
  --green-12: oklch(0.323 0.039 163.3); /* #203a2e */

  --amber-1: oklch(0.994 0.003 84.6); /* #fefdfb */
  --amber-2: oklch(0.98 0.024 88.2); /* #fff8e7 */
  --amber-3: oklch(0.956 0.048 85.8); /* #ffefcd */
  --amber-4: oklch(0.932 0.066 81.8); /* #ffe5b7 */
  --amber-5: oklch(0.904 0.086 78.3); /* #ffd99e */
  --amber-6: oklch(0.867 0.117 76.6); /* #ffc977 */
  --amber-7: oklch(0.824 0.1414 70.39); /* #ffb453 */
  --amber-8: oklch(0.7565 0.1641 69.75); /* #f19a00 */
  --amber-9: oklch(0.769 0.1647 70.08); /* #f59e0b */
  --amber-10: oklch(0.734 0.1603 68.78); /* #e99300 */
  --amber-11: oklch(0.574 0.13 64.2); /* #ac6500 */
  --amber-12: oklch(0.352 0.059 69.3); /* #4f3515 */

  --gray-1: oklch(0.991 0.003 264.5); /* #fbfcfe */
  --gray-2: oklch(0.981 0.006 255.5); /* #f6f9fd */
  --gray-3: oklch(0.956 0.01 252.8); /* #ecf1f7 */
  --gray-4: oklch(0.932 0.013 255.5); /* #e3e9f1 */
  --gray-5: oklch(0.91 0.016 257.2); /* #dbe2ec */
  --gray-6: oklch(0.888 0.019 255.5); /* #d2dbe7 */
  --gray-7: oklch(0.854 0.018 253.4); /* #c7d0db */
  --gray-8: oklch(0.795 0.019 253.4); /* #b4bdc8 */
  --gray-9: oklch(0.646 0.019 253.4); /* #868f9a */
  --gray-10: oklch(0.61 0.019 256.3); /* #7c848f */
  --gray-11: oklch(0.503 0.019 254); /* #5d656f */
  --gray-12: oklch(0.242 0.019 258.4); /* #1a2029 */

  /* two corners, one per job. --radius is the control's and the well's: a
     field, a button, a chip that is not a pill, a well inside a card.
     --radius-card is the container's: the card, and every layer that floats or
     sits over the page — dialog, menu, popover, select list, hovercard, toast.
     the ladder is closed otherwise (theme.css resets --radius-*); a third
     corner is a decision to take back to the system, not one to spell. */
  --radius: 0.375rem;
  --radius-card: 0.75rem;

  /* there is no --fg, and no -fg twin for any surface below: every one of them
     would resolve to gray-12. each surface below is light, so the ink never
     varies with the fill, and six names for one step is the shape the ramp
     exists to remove. body copy is text-gray-12 and de-emphasised
     copy is text-gray-11, at the call site, named as the rungs they are.
     a -fg name survives only where the ink genuinely follows its fill —
     --primary-fg, --destructive-fg, --success-fg, --warning-fg. those four are
     radix's per-ramp contrast token: three are white and --warning-fg is not,
     because amber's step 9 sits light enough to need dark ink. they share a
     value by coincidence of the ramps, not by duplication. */
  /* the surface model, outside in: page -> card -> well -> field, each on the
     radix step whose job it is (design-system.md, "Resting surfaces"):
     1-2 backgrounds, 3/4/5 a component at rest/hovered/pressed, 6 the edge of
     something you can't operate, 7/8 the edge of something you can, 9/10 a
     solid, 11/12 ink.
     the PAGE is --background (step 1), on every app and marketing page alike,
     painted once in platform's index.css. a CARD is step 2 with a step-6 edge
     and no shadow. a WELL (--panel) is step 3, one rung in from the card. a
     FIELD is step 1 (--surface) with the --input edge. a FLOATING layer —
     menu, popover, select list, hovercard, toast, and the dialog — is step 1
     (--popover) and keeps shadow-floating. */
  --background: var(--gray-1);
  /* the in-flow container: `card`, `solo-card`, the delegated-inset shells and
     the `.table` shell. step 2 — radix names "card background" there — with a
     --hairline edge, and no shadow: the step-6 edge is what finds it on the
     step-1 page, the marketing pages and a `--band` alike. */
  --card: var(--gray-2);
  /* a WELL inside a card: a recessed block that groups a figure, a meter
     track, a payout summary. step 3, one rung in from the card it sits in. */
  --panel: var(--gray-3);
  /* the edge of something you can't operate: a card's outline, a header's or
     footer's rule, a table's row lines, a divider between sections or list
     rows. step 6, radix's "subtle borders on components which are not
     interactive". not a control edge — that is --input. */
  --hairline: var(--gray-6);
  --primary: var(--blue-9); /* white-on-fill Lc 82.3 */
  /* the hovered rung of the filled control, and its pressed rung too. the ramp
     gives a solid fill two steps, 9 and 10; steps 11 and 12 are text and both
     sit LIGHTER than 10, so there is no third rung to press to. */
  --primary-hover: var(--blue-10);
  /* #ffffff — the ramp's own contrast color for the blue scale */
  --primary-fg: oklch(1 0 0);
  /* the dark brand ground: a full-bleed marketing hero, and the scrim that puts
     copy over a photograph. --primary is a control color tuned for white ink at
     Lc 82.3 — enough for a button, not enough to survive a translucent scrim over
     pixels you don't control. step 12 sits far enough down the ramp to carry
     --primary-fg with headroom (Lc 99.6), and headroom is what a scrim spends.
     at the 70% every hero scrim uses, over a white worst-case photograph, white
     ink lands at Lc 77.7 — clears the Lc 75 body text needs with 2.7 to spare.
     65% would be Lc 73.2 and fail; the Lc 75 line itself falls at 68% (Lc 75.9),
     so 70 is the nearest 5% step over the floor, not the floor itself. ink is
     --primary-fg; there is no -deep-fg, because a second name for #ffffff is a
     drift trap the test can't catch. */
  --primary-deep: var(--blue-12);
  /* the brand tint's rungs, one job each, on radix's roles. step 2 is a
     page-level GROUND — the full-bleed marketing band, which nothing hovers.
     steps 3/4/5 are a tinted ui element at rest / hovered / pressed or
     selected: a tinted chip rests on 3; a tinted option or row resting
     transparent hovers (or is highlighted) at 4 and is selected at 5 — a
     hovered row and a checked one have to paint differently or the state is
     invisible. a tinted surface presses UP the scale, not toward black, so
     every rung stays under its own ink. the neutral equivalents are the gray
     steps themselves (bg-gray-3/4/5), named at the call site. */
  --band: var(--blue-2);
  --secondary: var(--blue-3);
  --secondary-hover: var(--blue-4);
  --secondary-active: var(--blue-5);
  /* the filled error control: white ink at Lc 81.3. a tinted band carrying
     error copy takes --destructive-subtle/-fg below instead — that pair clears
     Lc 60 on its own band, which is a fill's job to do, not this one's. */
  --destructive: var(--red-9);
  /* hovered and pressed rung of the filled error control — one step for both,
     see --primary-hover. */
  --destructive-hover: var(--red-10);
  --destructive-fg: oklch(1 0 0); /* #ffffff */
  /* de-emphasised destructive surface: an error panel, banner, or row that
     carries error ink as body copy rather than a filled control. step 11 on
     step 3 is Lc 64.8, over the Lc 60 status ink needs. --destructive-subtle-fg
     is the error ink EVERYWHERE, the page included, not only on this band —
     --destructive is a fill, and step 9 read as text clears Lc 60 (Lc 74.1 on
     the page) only because red's step 9 happens to sit dark. green's clears it
     too (Lc 67.0) and amber's does not (Lc 39.9), so ink follows the rung, not
     the luck. an
     icon is a shape, not text, and keeps step 9. */
  --destructive-subtle: var(--red-3);
  --destructive-subtle-fg: var(--red-11);
  /* pressed rung for a control whose resting surface is --destructive-subtle.
     step 5 is the ramp's own active/selected rung. NOT the `color-mix(… 85%,
     black)` ladder the filled .btn variants use: on a near-white band that
     moves the surface away from the ink sitting on it and the pair fails. */
  --destructive-subtle-active: var(--red-5);
  /* white-on-fill Lc 74.3 — clears the Lc 60 a button label needs */
  --success: var(--green-9);
  /* hovered and pressed rung of the filled success control — one step for both,
     see --primary-hover. */
  --success-hover: var(--green-10);
  --success-fg: oklch(1 0 0); /* #ffffff */
  /* de-emphasised success surface, same shape as the destructive and warning
     bands: a confirmation panel, status pill, or row carrying success copy
     rather than a filled control. --success itself is a FILL and must never be
     painted on it — as text on the page it is Lc 67.0, clear of Lc 60 but under
     the Lc 75 body copy needs, and a step 9 is a fill by the ramp's rule either
     way; --success-subtle-fg is the success ink everywhere, Lc 66.1 here. step
     3, radix's component background: step 2 sits on the gray-2 card at 1.005:1
     and leaves a pill or badge no visible fill (WCAG 4.45:1, reference only —
     radix is the authority, PM rule 2026-11-01). an icon is a shape, not
     text, and keeps step 9. gray-12 on the band stays far clear, so it also takes
     neutral body copy. */
  --success-subtle: var(--green-3);
  --success-subtle-fg: var(--green-11);
  --warning: var(--amber-9); /* a fill, never text */
  /* hovered and pressed rung of the filled warning control — one step for both,
     see --primary-hover. a fill like --warning; --warning-fg is its ink. */
  --warning-hover: var(--amber-10);
  /* dark ink on the amber fill, Lc 52.1 — under the Lc 60 a button label
     needs, an accepted miss. not white: the palette tool emitted #fff for this
     scale (Lc 46.4, weaker still) while stock radix amber pairs dark text with
     it, so this is a generator artifact corrected, not a radix value
     overridden. */
  --warning-fg: var(--amber-12);
  /* de-emphasised warning surface: an advisory panel, banner, or row carrying
     warning copy rather than a filled control. --warning is a FILL and is not
     legible as text at any size; --warning-subtle-fg is the warning ink
     everywhere — step 12, not the ramp's 11: amber-11 on this band is 4.00:1,
     under the 4.5:1 warning copy needs; amber-12 is 9.98:1 (Lc 87.3). gray-12 on
     the band stays far clear, so it also takes neutral body copy. */
  --warning-subtle: var(--amber-3);
  --warning-subtle-fg: var(--amber-12);
  /* what a bare `border` draws: the base `*` rule reads it, and
     `surface-primary` rebinds it so a line inside a brand fill is drawn against
     that fill. step 6 at :root, the same rung as --hairline and the same job —
     a bare edge is a non-interactive one. the separate name exists for the
     rebind, which --hairline does not take. */
  --border: var(--gray-6);
  /* the edge of a field, checkbox, radio and select trigger: radix's role —
     step 7 is the interactive component's border, step 8 the hovered/stronger
     one. under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for an input's identifying boundary: 1.48:1
     on the card, 1.52:1 on the page, 1.37:1 in a well. an accepted miss by PM
     decision (2026-11-01), as the focus ring is — the field's label and
     placeholder, and its step-1 fill against the step-2 card, also identify
     it. fields and .btn-secondary share 7/8. */
  --input: var(--gray-7);
  /* the field edge under the pointer: radix's step 8, 1.80:1 on the card. */
  --input-hover: var(--gray-8);
  /* the fill a form control carries — radix's --color-surface. step 1, one
     rung lighter than the step-2 card, so a field reads as a recess-in-reverse
     on a card and lifts off a well by fill. the same value as --background and
     --popover doing a different job, so it keeps its own name.
     unrelated to the `surface-primary` utility, which is a brand-filled BAND.
     that one names what fills it; this one names what sits on a fill. */
  --surface: var(--gray-1);
  /* the floating fill: menu, popover, select list, hovercard, toast, and the
     dialog. step 1 with shadow-floating — radix themes' panel-plus-shadow —
     so a layer over a step-2 card reads lighter than it and above it. */
  --popover: var(--gray-1);
  /* step 8 is the ramp's focus rung, and deliberately not --primary: a ring
     that equals the fill it surrounds measures Lc 0.0 against it and is not
     there at all. on a --primary fill step 8 reaches Lc 30.0 — on the Lc 30 a
     focus indicator needs, not over it, which is the job the `surface-primary`
     utility keeps.
     against the page the ring is Lc 44.6, Lc 42.7 on the card — the rung
     radix assigns, taken as generated, and clear of Lc 30. in WCAG 2 terms
     it is 2.30:1 on the page and 2.24:1 on the card, under the 3:1 1.4.11
     asks of a state indicator: recorded in the ledger, not compensated here. */
  --ring: var(--blue-8);
  /* the scrim a dialog lays over the page — radix's --color-overlay. gray-12
     at 30%, which is what all four dialog backdrops already carried; naming it
     is what stops the fifth one being picked by eye. the dialog above it is
     --popover with shadow-floating — see the elevation set in
     packages/ui/src/styles/theme.css.
     every backdrop in the app spells it: the four ark backdrops, the dashboard
     drawer (a Modal size="none", so it takes the house backdrop rather than one
     of its own), and the one native <dialog>, whose backdrop: pseudo-element
     takes the same token. the docs site's embed playground spells it too; the
     only backdrop outside it is demo-nonprofit's, a page that impersonates a
     fictional org's website and would stop demonstrating that if it took a
     system token.
     color-mix() has no single literal, so this has no email twin — mail has no
     dialogs, so it needs none. */
  --overlay: color-mix(in oklch, var(--gray-12) 30%, transparent);
  /* ring + hairline for controls drawn ON a --primary fill.
     Lc 82.3 and about Lc 61 on --primary respectively — the second is a
     color-mix with no email twin and no checked value; read it out of a
     browser before leaning on the last digit. */
  --primary-ring: var(--primary-fg);
  --primary-border: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary-fg) 80%, var(--primary));

  --chart-1: oklch(0.646 0.222 41.116);
  --chart-2: oklch(0.6 0.118 184.704);
  --chart-3: oklch(0.398 0.07 227.392);
  --chart-4: oklch(0.828 0.189 84.429);
  --chart-5: oklch(0.769 0.188 70.08);
}
